**Continuous 2.38.8**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.7, 2.38.6, 2.38.5, 2.38.4, 2.38.3, 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.8.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.8.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.8.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.8.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.8.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.8.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.8.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.8-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.8.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.8-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.8.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.7

Settings is rebuilt. MCP servers have their own tab and are added in a dialog, not by editing a YAML file. Adding a model starts from what you have. Every model setting says whether you set it, and what happens when you did not. The Tools tab holds only tools.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent. Two requests now happen without a click: opening "Add a model" looks for model servers on this computer's usual ports, and a connection is tested when you paste a key or pick a server (it lists the models, which costs nothing).

### New

- **MCP servers tab.** The second Settings tab. Each server shows whether it is saved for all your projects or for this workspace, and its menu has Edit, Move, Duplicate and Remove. A server that did not start says why, with Edit and Try again.
- **Add an MCP server in a dialog.** Paste a command line, a URL, or the JSON other tools use, and the form fills in. Choose where to save it: for all your projects, or for this workspace only. Advanced options are folded, and each says what happens when you leave it alone. Test starts the server without saving and shows the tools it offers. A value that looks like a credential is kept as a secret, never in a workspace file.
- **Set a whole MCP server's tools at once.** A menu on each server sets every tool to Ask First or Automatic. Excluded tools and tools still waiting for approval are left alone.
- **Add a model.** It asks what you have: an API key, a server on this computer (found ones are listed), a server on your network, or nothing yet. The model list shows context size, price and tool support. A "Use for" step says what will change, for example "Chat: currently Claude Sonnet → will be llama3.1:8b".
- **A model's Overview.** The first tab of a model's Configure dialog shows each value in use and where it comes from: set by you, an account, the provider, the server, published, or assumed.
- **Set by you, or not set.** In the model dialog every field reads "Set by you" with Reset, or "Not set" with what happens then. The word "Default" on its own is gone from the model dialog, the per-mode table and the Thinking menu.
- **A delay for IDGAF.** IDGAF is the top level of each area and the preset that puts them all there, with a delay of 0. Set the delay to 5 or 10 seconds in the Decision timer, and a call that runs only because of IDGAF is shown first, with Run now and Don't run. Calls that a lower level would have run anyway are never delayed.
- **With Continue installed too.** One notice, once, says that Continuous keeps its own configuration and that both extensions bind the same shortcuts, with a button to the Keyboard Shortcuts editor.
- **Terminal agent: failures say more.** A call to a tool that does not exist is answered with the tools that do, and the editor's names for the same tools are accepted.

### Behaviour changes

- **Settings tabs.** Models, MCP servers, Tools, Permissions, Rules, Configs, General, Help. Providers is part of Models. "Settings" is now "General", with Indexing folded into it. The approval levels, built-in rules, decision timer, shadow review and "Commands and secrets" moved from Tools to Permissions. Old links still open the right place. The gear opens Models when no chat model is selected, and otherwise the tab you used last.
- **Plan mode asks on both surfaces.** In the terminal agent, a command that changes state used to run in Plan mode at the Permissive level or under an allow rule. It now asks, as the editor already did. At the Automatic level the reviewer is no longer consulted for such a call in Plan mode; you are asked.
- **A Loop item stops at its question limit.** With four questions open, a further call that needs approval ends the item's run as waiting. It starts again when you answer.
- **Local servers and output length.** An OpenAI-compatible server on this computer or network with no known output limit is no longer sent a limit of 4,096 tokens. The server decides. A limit you set is always sent.
- **MCP tool call timeout.** It has its own setting, `toolTimeout`, 60 seconds when not set. A config that sets only `connectionTimeout` behaves as before.
- **Failed and refused tool calls.** The model is told why an edit did not change the file, what was kept, and what to do next. The closing line "Please try something else or request further instructions" is gone.
- **Container mode.** With `terminal.shell` set to `container`, `.git/hooks`, `.git/config`, `.vscode`, `.envrc` and similar files are read-only inside the container. `git config` and `git remote add` fail there.
- **Remote windows.** In an SSH or dev container window with `terminal.shell` set to `wsl` or `container`, the terminal tool does not run the command and says which setting to change. A WSL remote window with `wsl` set is unaffected.
- **Run on a code block.** The text typed into the terminal must be one line of plain text. A block whose command is empty or holds a control character shows a warning and types nothing.
- **Heads-up buttons.** A call shown before it runs has "Run now" and "Don't run" where it had "Accept" and "Reject".
- **The IDGAF chip** says only "IDGAF".

### Fixes

- **Scrolling a long chat.** A jump through a chat of 1,000 messages took about 170 ms a step and now takes about 30. Messages on screen no longer shift while you scroll.
- **Short panels.** With approvals, tasks and queued messages waiting in a short panel, the chat keeps about 100 pixels and the prompt stays in view. The command being approved shows directly above Accept and Reject.
- **Narrow sidebar.** Every Settings tab is reachable below 330 pixels; six were hidden behind a sideways scroll. Settings rows, the Loop panel and the blocked-calls list wrap where they ran off the side.
- **Switches and the keyboard.** The switches in Settings could not be reached with Tab. They can, and Space or Enter works them.
- **A diff rejected in the editor.** Rejecting a diff from its code lens or shortcut left the call running, and the model was told the edit succeeded. It is told you rejected it.
- **MCP working directory on Windows.** A working directory given as a drive path was ignored. It is used.
- **The chat page and commands.** The page can no longer make the extension run a host command on its own, and a Loop check runs only against a decision recorded for that exact command.
